Background: Experts agree that knowing when AI will be able to perform on the same level as humans in most or all fields is important, but there is much less consensus on how to define an AI that reaches that milestone. Here, we offer one potential definition of AGI focused on AI systems’ ability to replace all but the best humans at nearly all non-physical tasks that generate economic value and are paid for in today’s labor market.

Resolution Criteria: Ground Truth. FRI - LEAP Panel

- “Professional employee” refers to a trained or experienced worker. To satisfy this question’s criteria, a system must perform at or above the level of the 90th percentile of such human workers in 2025, across all sectors. To qualify, the system should be able to replace individual human employees with the same level of support and supervision required for a 90th percentile human in the occupation in 2025.
- “Economically useful non-physical occupation” refers to work for which there is a paying market and where the worker’s value-add is dominated by cognitive rather than physical skills.
    - These occupations are dominated by analytical and creative tasks such as reasoning, planning, learning new information, communication, and decision-making.
    - For the purposes of this question, roles that are in-scope include: doctors and nurses, lawyers and legal aids, project managers, and AI/robotics researchers.
    - Roles that are out-of-scope include construction laborers, police officers, factory line workers, professional athletes, and electricians.
    - You should consider these roles as they existed at the end of 2025, even if you expect future versions of them to involve human-AI interaction to a much greater degree than they do currently.
    - To satisfy this question’s criteria, a system must outperform the 90th percentile 2025 human on at least 90% of the non-physical tasks associated with the role.
- The system must be commercially available, general, and no more than 5x as costly as equivalent human labor.
    - A system is considered “commercially available” if it can be purchased or licensed by firms or individuals (or is freely available), rather than being restricted to internal research use.
    - The system must be general - i.e., a single system that can reach the required level of performance across all relevant occupations.
    - To qualify, the AI's inference cost for replacing the labor of a given human professional must be within 5x of the equivalent human labor cost. For example, the AI inference cost necessary to replace a human’s yearly output must be no more than 5x their salary.
- This question will be resolved by FRI surveying the LEAP panel, or another expert panel with similar representation as LEAP.
    - We will ask them the following question and include the same definitions as provided above: “Imagine occupations as they were in 2025, focused on those whose economic value-add was primarily non-physical. Thinking of today’s AI systems, is there a commercially available system that could have performed as well or better than the 90th percentile professional employee in those 2025 occupations at no more than 5x the cost?” 
    - The LEAP panel estimate is computed by weighting the four expert categories (computer science, AI industry, economics, policy) equally, and then adjusting for demographic characteristics within each category. If the LEAP panel is not available by the resolution date, FRI will recruit a similar expert panel to resolve the question.

label: Opus 5
rationale: I anchored the catastrophe questions on LEAP Wave 9 (May-Jun 2026), whose expert unconditional medians are 0.3%/2%/5% for an AI-caused 10%-mortality catastrophe and 1%/4.2%/10% for any such catastrophe by 2030/2050/2100, shading toward the better-calibrated superforecaster numbers (0.1%/0.88%/2.4% for AI) to land at ~0.18%/1.9%/4.8% (AI) and ~0.65%/3.8%/9% (any). The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. My own inputs: combined OpenAI+Anthropic run-rate is already ~$105B, so I put end-2030 at p50 ~$360B; frontier ECI grew ~1.5-2.2 points/month over the past year, giving ~179 by March 2027; and Expert AGI as LEAP defines it (90th-percentile professional across all non-physical occupations, <=5x cost, panel-adjudicated) I place at 88% before 2100 with a median of 2042 — earlier than the LEAP expert median of 2050 but later than lab leaders, reflecting the panel-agreement lag.

rationale: I anchored the catastrophe questions on LEAP Wave 9 (May-Jun 2026), whose expert unconditional medians are 0.3%/2%/5% for an AI-caused 10%-mortality catastrophe and 1%/4.2%/10% for any such catastrophe by 2030/2050/2100, shading toward the better-calibrated superforecaster numbers (0.1%/0.88%/2.4% for AI) to land at ~0.18%/1.9%/4.8% (AI) and ~0.65%/3.8%/9% (any). The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. rationale: I anchored the catastrophe questions on LEAP Wave 9 (May-Jun 2026), whose expert unconditional medians are 0.3%/2%/5% for an AI-caused 10%-mortality catastrophe and 1%/4.2%/10% for any such catastrophe by 2030/2050/2100, shading toward the better-calibrated superforecaster numbers (0.1%/0.88%/2.4% for AI) to land at ~0.18%/1.9%/4.8% (AI) and ~0.65%/3.8%/9% (any). The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. My own inputs: combined OpenAI+Anthropic run-rate is already ~$105B, so I put end-2030 at p50 ~$360B; frontier ECI grew ~1.5-2.2 points/month over the past year, giving ~179 by March 2027; and Expert AGI as LEAP defines it (90th-percentile professional across all non-physical occupations, <=5x cost, panel-adjudicated) I place at 88% before 2100 with a median of 2042 — earlier than the LEAP expert median of 2050 but later than lab leaders, reflecting the panel-agreement lag.

The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. My own inputs: combined OpenAI+Anthropic run-rate is already ~$105B, so I put end-2030 at p50 ~$360B; frontier ECI grew ~1.5-2.2 points/month over the past year, giving ~179 by March 2027; and Expert AGI as LEAP defines it (90th-percentile professional across all non-physical occupations, <=5x cost, panel-adjudicated) I place at 88% before 2100 with a median of 2042 — earlier than the LEAP expert median of 2050 but later than lab leaders, reflecting the panel-agreement lag.

rationale: I anchored the catastrophe questions on LEAP Wave 9 (May-Jun 2026), whose expert unconditional medians are 0.3%/2%/5% for an AI-caused 10%-mortality catastrophe and 1%/4.2%/10% for any such catastrophe by 2030/2050/2100, shading toward the better-calibrated superforecaster numbers (0.1%/0.88%/2.4% for AI) to land at ~0.18%/1.9%/4.8% (AI) and ~0.65%/3.8%/9% (any). The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. My own inputs: combined OpenAI+Anthropic run-rate is already ~$105B, so I put end-2030 at p50 ~$360B; frontier ECI grew ~1.5-2.2 points/month over the past year, giving ~179 by March 2027; and Expert AGI as LEAP defines it (90th-percentile professional across all non-physical occupations, <=5x cost, panel-adjudicated) I place at 88% before 2100 with a median of 2042 — earlier than the LEAP expert median of 2050 but later than lab leaders, reflecting the panel-agreement lag.

rationale: I anchored the catastrophe questions on LEAP Wave 9 (May-Jun 2026), whose expert unconditional medians are 0.3%/2%/5% for an AI-caused 10%-mortality catastrophe and 1%/4.2%/10% for any such catastrophe by 2030/2050/2100, shading toward the better-calibrated superforecaster numbers (0.1%/0.88%/2.4% for AI) to land at ~0.18%/1.9%/4.8% (AI) and ~0.65%/3.8%/9% (any). The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. My own inputs: combined OpenAI+Anthropic run-rate is already ~$105B, so I put end-2030 at p50 ~$360B; frontier ECI grew ~1.5-2.2 points/month over the past year, giving ~179 by March 2027; and Expert AGI as LEAP defines it (90th-percentile professional across all non-physical occupations, <=5x cost, panel-adjudicated) I place at 88% before 2100 with a median of 2042 — earlier than the LEAP expert median of 2050 but later than lab leaders, reflecting the panel-agreement lag.

rationale: I anchored the catastrophe questions on LEAP Wave 9 (May-Jun 2026), whose expert unconditional medians are 0.3%/2%/5% for an AI-caused 10%-mortality catastrophe and 1%/4.2%/10% for any such catastrophe by 2030/2050/2100, shading toward the better-calibrated superforecaster numbers (0.1%/0.88%/2.4% for AI) to land at ~0.18%/1.9%/4.8% (AI) and ~0.65%/3.8%/9% (any). The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. My own inputs: combined OpenAI+Anthropic run-rate is already ~$105B, so I put end-2030 at p50 ~$360B; frontier ECI grew ~1.5-2.2 points/month over the past year, giving ~179 by March 2027; and Expert AGI as LEAP defines it (90th-percentile professional across all non-physical occupations, <=5x cost, panel-adjudicated) I place at 88% before 2100 with a median of 2042 — earlier than the LEAP expert median of 2050 but later than lab leaders, reflecting the panel-agreement lag.

rationale: I anchored the catastrophe questions on LEAP Wave 9 (May-Jun 2026), whose expert unconditional medians are 0.3%/2%/5% for an AI-caused 10%-mortality catastrophe and 1%/4.2%/10% for any such catastrophe by 2030/2050/2100, shading toward the better-calibrated superforecaster numbers (0.1%/0.88%/2.4% for AI) to land at ~0.18%/1.9%/4.8% (AI) and ~0.65%/3.8%/9% (any). The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. The incident ladders are cumulative over all qualifying incidents in the onset window, so the low rungs are dominated by economic damages rather than deaths: with AI-powered social engineering already implicated in ~85% of insured cyber losses in H1 2026, IC3 losses forecast at $27-55B, and IBM finding 1-in-4 breaches AI-enabled, cumulative AI-related cyber damages above $220M and $2.2B are near-certain, ~$22B likely, and $220B roughly even-money by 2030, with the ladder then falling steeply once mass-casualty pathways must carry it. Misalignment rungs start from a live base rate — the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent breakout, three Anthropic eval escapes into real third-party systems, and 44 documented misalignment incidents in METR's May 2026 report — so $220M cumulative by 2030 is likely, while the AI-bio ladder starts far lower (CB-1 uplift but no realized AI-enabled outbreak, and wet-lab/materials bottlenecks plus tightening synthesis screening) and grows mostly over the 2050/2100 horizons. Conditionally, I treated revenue, AGI year and March-2027 ECI as correlated indicators of capability, deployment scale and adaptation time, applying odds multipliers that are strongest at short horizons and high severities and largest for the most capability-elastic categories (bio, misalignment, disempowerment) and weakest for the already-saturated low cyber rungs; ECI 162-168 read as a near-stall given the frontier already sits at ~169 (GPT-6 Astra), so they cut risk sharply. My own inputs: combined OpenAI+Anthropic run-rate is already ~$105B, so I put end-2030 at p50 ~$360B; frontier ECI grew ~1.5-2.2 points/month over the past year, giving ~179 by March 2027; and Expert AGI as LEAP defines it (90th-percentile professional across all non-physical occupations, <=5x cost, panel-adjudicated) I place at 88% before 2100 with a median of 2042 — earlier than the LEAP expert median of 2050 but later than lab leaders, reflecting the panel-agreement lag.
